asof: Settles Wed 28 Oct 2026 · written Thu 29 Oct
headline: Fed holds 10–2 with two hike dissents and no rush; SR3 rallies 4–5bp in H7–U7. U7 peak 4.645% still beats consensus.
summary: The strip rallied after the FOMC, led by the 2027 contracts: H7 and M7 fell 5.5bp in implied rate, U7 4.5bp and Z7 3.5bp, while U6 and Z6 eased only 1bp and the 2029 contracts rose 1–2bp. That undid most of Tuesday's selloff but not the week: M7 and U7 are still 2.5bp and 3.5bp higher since Friday, and the 2028–29 contracts 3.5–4.5bp higher. Month to date the rally is intact, with Z6 11bp and Z7 24.7bp lower than the end-September (modelled) settles. The peak is SR3U7 at 4.645%, 69.5bp over the latest 3.95% SOFR fixing, with only 13bp of easing priced from there to Z9; most forecasters see one more hike in December and a peak near 4.00–4.25%.
drivers: A divided hold, with no urgency

The FOMC held at 3.75–4.00% by 10–2, with Governor Cook and Cleveland's Hammack dissenting for a hike, and swapped September's hike language for a line about gathering more information. Warsh stressed that inflation is too high but that expectations are anchored and the economy is not overheating, so the market read no pressure to move beyond December: H7 and M7 fell 5.5bp in rate and the 2-year Treasury yield ended about 3bp lower near 4.71%.

The 10-year rose about 3bp to near 5.02% and the 30-year almost 5bp, led by breakevens, and the SR3 strip pivoted the same way: Z8 to Z9 rose 0.5–2bp in rate, so Z7/Z8 widened 4bp and U7/Z8 5bp. Warsh also said one of the eight 2027 meetings, and two in 2028, will carry no rate decision, a small cut in the number of live dates.

Brent settled $1.44 higher at $115.32 and WTI $2.88 higher at $102.78 after a Houthi strike claim on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and a report that the US told Gulf states to prepare for a short campaign after the midterms. That capped the rally in the 2028–29 contracts and keeps an energy-driven inflation risk under the 2027 hikes.
Front end anchored by firm funding

SOFR printed 3.95% for 27 October, 7bp over EFFR and 5bp over IORB, with the 99th percentile at 4.04%, ahead of the 30 October Canadian year-end and MBS paydown date; U6 and Z6 moved only 1bp. The $30bn 2-year FRN cleared at a 0.038% high margin (0.04% last time) with indirects taking 71%, a sign of strong cash demand for floaters.
spreads: The whites flattened as 2027 rallied and December held: Z6/H7 narrowed 4.5bp to +23.5bp (−8.1bp month to date) and Z6/M7 4.5bp to +39.5bp (−10.9bp), while U6/Z6 was flat at +26.7bp and H7/M7 flat at +16bp. M7/U7 widened 1bp to +6bp and U7/Z7 1bp to −1.5bp, so the peak stays in U7. Z6/Z7 narrowed 2.5bp to +44bp, still 2bp wider on the week but 13.7bp narrower than at end-September. The reds and greens steepened back on the long-end selloff: Z7/Z8 +4bp to −7bp, U7/Z8 +5bp to −8.5bp and Z8/Z9 +1.5bp to −4.5bp; there is no month-to-date base before 20 October for these. Flies were quiet: H7/M7/U7 fell 1bp to +10bp and M7/U7/Z7 was flat at +7.5bp (+1.5bp on the week).
fed: Fed funds futures were last recorded at Tuesday's close, before the decision: they carried 2bp for Wednesday (8% odds of a hike), 22.4bp cumulative by December with an 83% chance of at least one hike, 49.6bp by March, 69.5bp by June and a 75.5bp peak at the September 2027 FOMC (implied EFFR 4.635%). That compares with 23.4bp, 48.6bp and a 72bp peak a day earlier, 25.8bp, 55.2bp and 81bp a week ago, and 30.6bp, 63.4bp and a 94bp peak at end-September. SR3 has since moved: U7 at 4.645% is only 1bp over that ZQ peak despite a 7bp SOFR–EFFR gap in the latest fixing, so Wednesday's rally has already taken a few bp of 2027 hikes out that ZQ has not yet recorded. Forecasters remain lower: most economists expect one more hike in December and a 4.00–4.25% peak, and the September median dot was 4.1% for both end-2026 and end-2027, against close to 50bp of further 2027 tightening in the strip.

ideas.title: Sell the Z6/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open and 1.5bp against at +39.5bp, after narrowing 4.5bp on the FOMC; the stop at +48bp is 8.5bp away and the spread is 10.9bp narrower than at end-September. The meeting supports the case: December is the only hike the Fed and most economists see, which Z6 already holds, while M7 still carries the second and third hikes a no-urgency Fed has not signalled. Levels unchanged.
ideas.risk: A hot core PCE or ECI this week would revive 2027 hikes and push the spread back toward the +48bp stop.

ideas.title: Buy 2028 easing: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open and 1bp against at −7bp: Wednesday's rally lifted Z7 3.5bp in price while Z8 slipped 0.5bp, so the hedge gave back 4bp as the core gained 4.5bp, doing its job. Only 13bp of easing is priced from the U7 peak to Z9, little if the Fed takes SOFR toward 4.6% with Brent at $115. Keep at about half the core size; stop +2bp, target −25bp.
ideas.risk: A further long-end selloff on term premium or fiscal worries around the midterms would push the spread through the stop.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through month-end

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 rallied 1bp to 3.923% implied, but SOFR printed 3.95% for 27 October, above that average, and the 30 October year-end and MBS dates could hold fixings firm, so a long has little to gain. With the October meeting gone, only the 9 December decision touches U6, and only for its final week; revisit after month-end prints.
ideas.risk: A soft funding turn with SOFR back near 3.88% would leave a few bp of upside on the table.

watch: Core PCE seen at 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y, GDP near 3.0% (GDPNow 3.3%); a hot core print would undo Wednesday's H7–U7 rally.
Q3 employment cost index, Chicago PMI, month-end
Canadian year-end and MBS paydowns test SOFR's 3.95% print; wage costs matter for the 2027 hikes.
Prices paid was 77.9 in September; note settlement drains cash from repo.
Fiscal outlook and term premium for the reds and greens; Gulf strike risk is reported for after the vote.
September added only 29,000; a soft report would extend the 2027 rally, a firm one the selloff.
Brent at $115.32 is the main risk to fading 2027 hikes; $120 is the pain point.
